title: Mr Bates vs The Post Office and the Offences Act (2024)

steps.claim: ITV airs Mr Bates vs The Post Office over four nights

test.source: ITV broadcast, 1–4 Jan 2024

steps.claim: Attention to the Horizon scandal surges
A petition to strip Paula Vennells of her CBE passes a million signatures

test.source: Change.org petition count reported by the BBC, 8 Jan 2024

steps.link_why: coverage tied the petition's growth to the drama

steps.claim: Vennells hands back her CBE

test.source: Paula Vennells statement, 9 Jan 2024

steps.link_why: her statement followed the petition and the broadcast

steps.claim: The Prime Minister announces a law to quash the convictions

test.source: Hansard, 10 Jan 2024 (Post Office Horizon Scandal statement)

steps.link_why: ministers later credited the drama's effect on public outcry (Hansard, 20 Mar 2024)

steps.claim: At the Offences Bill's second reading, MPs credit the drama with the public outcry

test.source: Hansard, 20 Mar 2024: 'that powerful ITV drama … prompted a public outcry'; 'the influence of the ITV drama … has been very significant in this campaign'

steps.link_why: the debate names the drama as the trigger

steps.claim: The Post Office (Horizon System) Offences Act 2024 quashes the convictions

test.source: Post Office (Horizon System) Offences Act 2024, Royal Assent 24 May 2024

steps.link_why: the second-reading debate credits the drama's role in the campaign
steps.note: The Act quashed convictions in England and Wales; Scotland and Northern Ireland passed their own Acts. The campaign and the public inquiry predate the drama by years; the drama is credited with the speed of the political response.

steps.claim: Hundreds of convictions are quashed and compensation payments follow
steps.note: Convictions were quashed automatically on Royal Assent; compensation offers followed through 2024.

steps.claim: Attention to Paula Vennells surges

title: Cathy Come Home and the homelessness law (1966)

steps.claim: The BBC broadcasts Cathy Come Home to 12 million viewers

test.source: BBC Wednesday Play, 16 Nov 1966; audience figure cited in Hansard, 15 Dec 1966

steps.claim: Shelter launches two weeks later

test.source: Shelter founded 1 Dec 1966

steps.note: Shelter was planned before the broadcast; the play gave its launch a national audience.

steps.claim: MPs cite the play in the Housing Subsidies Bill debate

test.source: Hansard, 15 Dec 1966: 'the conscience of the nation has been jolted by a television play … Cathy Come Home'

steps.link_why: the speech names the play as the jolt

steps.claim: The Housing (Homeless Persons) Act 1977 creates a statutory duty to house people in priority need

test.source: Housing (Homeless Persons) Act 1977, Royal Assent 29 Jul 1977 (Stephen Ross's private member's bill)

steps.link_why: Hansard, 28 Oct 2016: the play 'coincided with the launch of Shelter and eventually led to the passage of the Housing (Homeless Persons) Act 1977'
steps.note: Eleven years is a long ripple; the link is Parliament's own account, not a measurement.

steps.claim: Councils must house priority-need households from December 1977

test.source: Act commenced 1 Dec 1977 in England and Wales

title: Quincy, M.E. and the Orphan Drug Act (1981)

steps.claim: Quincy episode 'Seldom Silent, Never Heard' dramatizes Tourette's and the drugs no company will make

test.source: NBC broadcast, 4 Mar 1981

steps.claim: Jack Klugman testifies to Congress on orphan drugs

test.source: House Subcommittee on Health and the Environment hearing, 9 Mar 1981

steps.link_why: the hearing followed the episode; Klugman appeared as the show's star

steps.claim: A second episode, 'Give Me Your Weak', airs as the bill stalls

test.source: NBC broadcast, 10 Mar 1982

steps.link_why: the episode was written to push the stalled bill

steps.claim: The Orphan Drug Act is signed

test.source: Public Law 97-414, signed 4 Jan 1983

steps.link_why: accounts credit the two episodes with helping the Act pass (Henry Waxman; Hal Erickson)
steps.note: Waxman's bill predates the first episode; the show is credited with the public pressure that passed it.

steps.claim: Hundreds of orphan drugs reach approval

test.source: FDA: more than 600 orphan-designated drugs and biologics approved since 1983, against about 10 in the decade before

steps.link_why: the FDA attributes the approvals to the Act's incentives

title: My Octopus Teacher and the Sentience Act (2020)

steps.claim: Netflix releases My Octopus Teacher

test.source: Netflix release, 7 Sep 2020

steps.claim: Attention to octopus intelligence rises
The film wins the Academy Award for Documentary Feature

test.source: 93rd Academy Awards, 25 Apr 2021

steps.link_why: the award is the film's own

steps.claim: A minister tells the Lords he was 'profoundly affected' by the film during the Sentience Bill

test.source: Hansard, 20 Jul 2021, Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill [HL]

steps.link_why: the minister names the film from the Dispatch Box

steps.claim: Octopuses, crabs and lobsters are added to the bill after an LSE review

test.source: Defra announcement and the LSE review, 19 Nov 2021

steps.note: The review was commissioned separately; the film's part is attention, not evidence.

steps.claim: The Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act 2022 receives Royal Assent

test.source: Royal Assent 28 Apr 2022

steps.note: The Act was coming regardless; whether the film moved the cephalopod decision is unproven.

steps.claim: 60 Minutes airs 'Insiders' on members of Congress trading stock

test.source: CBS, 13 Nov 2011

steps.claim: Cosponsors of the STOCK Act jump from 9 to more than 100 within weeks

test.source: Congress.gov cosponsor dates for H.R. 1148, Nov–Dec 2011

steps.link_why: the cosponsor dates cluster in the weeks after the broadcast

steps.claim: The Senate passes the bill 96–3

test.source: Senate roll call, 2 Feb 2012

steps.claim: The STOCK Act is signed

test.source: Public Law 112-105, signed 4 Apr 2012

steps.link_why: the Act's history records that it 'gained popularity following a 60 Minutes segment'
steps.note: The bill had been introduced in 2006 and reintroduced in March 2011; the segment is credited with its passage, not its existence.

steps.claim: Members' trades must be disclosed within 45 days

test.source: STOCK Act periodic transaction reports begin, July 2012
